analysis.title: Krona gains ground - tonight's earnings in focus
key_insights: Market moves were modest on 10/20 with no major data or earnings. European equities mostly declined, weighed down by energy and unrest and debt concerns in France. The S&P 500 gained 0.3% and the Nasdaq was broadly unchanged.
Asian markets are more positive this morning on a relatively strong start to earnings season. Equity futures point to higher opens in Europe and the US.
Reuters reports 13% of S&P 500 companies have reported so far, of which 86% beat earnings forecasts. Meta and Tesla report after the US close tonight and could be a stronger market catalyst.
French bond yields paused their rise while yields elsewhere were broadly unchanged. Expectations of a Fed rate hike next week eased further after weak September home sales and construction activity.
The dollar weakened against all other G10 currencies, with modest moves, extending October's consolidation after strong September gains.
Brent crude is trading close to USD 110 per barrel again, after briefly falling on reports of renewed peace talks that were subsequently denied.
German PPI, the most important release on 10/20, rose further as expected, driven by high energy prices.

The Trump administration announced USD 8 billion in fuel subsidies for farmers facing rising diesel prices, ahead of midterm elections. US envoy Steve Witkoff is due to meet Putin today as the US pushes to end the war in Ukraine.
In the Alberta referendum, 76% voted against starting a process towards independence, per unofficial results.

UK September CPI is due today. Headline and core are both expected to edge higher, supporting SEB's and market expectations of a Bank of England rate hike on 5 November. The UK budget is next week, and the government must address high public debt and a large deficit. The FT reports Chancellor Healey will not raise capital gains tax.

EUR/SEK has turned lower in October after an almost uninterrupted rise in August and September. The carry-favouring market environment was a headwind for the krona in autumn, made worse because the yen has been used less as a funding currency due to FX intervention.

Eased Fed and other central bank rate hike expectations weakened the dollar against most G10 currencies including the krona. Euro weakness from France's problems made the EUR/SEK decline more pronounced.

A sustained krona strengthening needs more foreign central banks moving toward policy normalisation rather than further hikes, or markets pricing such a shift. SEB says this probably requires a more persistent disinflationary contribution from energy prices.

The National Institute of Economic Research's Wage Formation Report, published at 09:00 today, concludes higher corporate productivity gives favourable conditions for real wage growth over the next few years, per Swedish Radio.

The yen has been used less as a funding currency this autumn because of FX intervention.
geopolitical: Unrest and debt concerns in France weighed on European equities and the euro, and French bond yields have been rising.
